text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Paper maker KNP BT takes over German, Italian wholesalers from Britain's plastics and paper group Bunzl. (p1)
- Rotterdam chamber of commerce seeks to expand existing pipeline network between Rotterdam and Antwerp. Maybe used to transport ethylene (p1)
- Junior finance minister Wim Vermeend contacts OECD colleagues to tackle Internet tax loophole. (p1)
- Consumer confidence falls slightly in December. (p1)
- Rabobank is only bank with S&P triple-A rating. (p1)
- Steel wholesaler Dikema & Chabot buys steel maker Hoogovens' reinforced steel unit Wapeningsstaal Trading. (p3)
- Entertainment firm Endemol and U.S. theatrical producer Dodge Productions near accord on starting joint venture. (p3) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch soccer association (KNVB) halts negotiating TV rights for its members. (p1)
- Cacao De Zaan cocoa plant welcomes new U.S. owner Archer Daniels Midland. (p2)
- Food/drinks group BolsWessanen buys Britain's breakfast cereals firm Barber Chestergate. (p2)
- Publisher Elsevier emerges as best investment over last 30 years -- Amsterdam university research. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Guests at Amsterdam's Grand Hotel Krasnapolsky flee from kitchen fire. (p1)
- Radar and weapon systems maker Holland Signaal takes over three operations from Deutsche System-Technik (DST). (p27)
- Growing number of non-profit groups start temp agency. (p27)
- Chemicals giant DSM launches staff motivation drive, dubbed Vita. (p27) TROUW
- Dutch companies R&D spend at 1.08 pct of GDP in 1995 versus 1.26 pct in 1986. (p4)
- New conflict between unions and banks. ING and Generale try to exclude some staff from conditions and pay deal. (p4) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch companies play increasing role in cross-border mergers and takeovers. (p1)
- Builder IHC Caland to participate in building world's largest floating oil production and storage system. (p13)
